IMPORTANT PUBLIC HEALTH AND SAFETY MESSAGE REGARDING
PARTICIPATION AT CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS
AS A RESULT OF THE COVID-19 VIRUS, AND RESULTING ORDERS AND DIRECTION FROM THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES, THE GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AND THE ORANGE COUNTY HEALTH CARE AGENCY, AS WELL AS THE CITY OF IRVINE EMERGENCY DECLARATION, THE PUBLIC WILL NOT BE PERMITTED TO PHYSICALLY ATTEND THE IRVINE CITY COUNCIL MEETING TO WHICH THIS AGENDA APPLIES.
YOU MAY SUBMIT COMMENTS ON ANY AGENDA ITEM OR ON ANY ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA, IN WRITING VIA MAIL TO “ATTN: CITY COUNCIL,” ONE CIVIC CENTER PLAZA, IRVINE, CA 92606; BY EMAIL TO CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG; OR THROUGH E-COMMENT AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. YOU MAY WATCH THE MEETING LIVE ON ICTV, COX COMMUNICATIONS LOCAL ACCESS CHANNEL 30, AND AT&T U-VERSE CHANNEL 99, AND LIVESTREAMED ONLINE AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV.
PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. IT WOULD BE APPRECIATED IF COMMUNICATIONS OF PUBLIC COMMENTS RELATED TO ITEMS ON THE AGENDA, OR ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA, ARE PROVIDED PRIOR TO THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE MEETING. IF THAT IS NOT POSSIBLE, EVERY EFFORT WILL BE MADE TO ATTEMPT TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS DURING THE COURSE OF THE MEETING. TOWARDS THIS END, THE MAYOR WILL ENDEAVOR TO TAKE A BRIEF PAUSE BEFORE ACTION IS TAKEN ON ANY AGENDA ITEM TO ALLOW THE CITY CLERK TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS, AND SHARE ANY E-COMMENTS RECEIVED DURING THE MEETING.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council and Successor Agency meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council and/or Successor Agency meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council/Successor Agency meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv. For more information, please contact the City Clerk's office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council/Successor Agency will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council/Successor Agency meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council/Successor Agency meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council/Successor Agency meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council/Successor Agency regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk's Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council/Successor Agency Board.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE

  CALL TO ORDER

  The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council and regular joint meeting with the City of
  Irvine as Successor Agency to the dissolved Irvine Redevelopment Agency was called to
  order at 4:12 p.m. on Decembers, 2020, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center,
  One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California; Mayor/Chairwoman Khan presiding.

  ROLL CALL

  Present:  Councilmember/Boardmember:  Larry Agran
  Councilmember/Boardmember:  Tammy Kim
  CouncilmemberBoardmember:  Anthony Kuo
  Vice MayorA/ice Chairman:  Mike Carroll
  Mayor/Chairwoman  Farrah N. Khan

  Communications Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and
  livestreamed online at cityofirvine.org\ and that in an effort to protect public health and
  prevent the spread of COVID-19, the e-comment feature had been extended for all
  agenda items, which allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments
  through the public comment portion of each item and would be included as part of the
  official record and uploaded to the City's website. She also assured the community that
  the City of Irvine was adhering to the Governor's Executive Order in the Council Chamber
  and throughout City Hall by sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face
  masks.
 City Council Minutes  December 8. 2020

  Mayor/Chairwoman Khan also announced that general public comments for the City
  Council on items not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.,

  appreciation for everyone's patience and understanding as the City continued to make
  adjustments to meeting protocols as needed.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Mayor Khan made the following announcements:

  • The Irvine 2/11 Marine Adoption Committee's annual Holiday Toy Drive supports
  the families of Irvine's adopted 2/11 Marine Battalion. Members of the community
  can still help bring joy to these families during the holidays by donating an
  unwrapped gift suitable for an infant or child age 12 or younger. Donations will be
  accepted through December 14 at City Hall, the Irvine Police Department, and the
  Orange County Great Park Visitor Center. There will also be a drive-thru, drop-off
  event on Saturday, December 12 from 9 a.m. to noon at the Irvine Civic Center.
  Monetary donations and donations through AmazonSmile are also being
  accepted. To donate online and for more information, visit cityofirvine.org/211.

  • In observance of the Christmas holiday, non-emergency City services will be
  closed Thursday, December 24 and Friday, December 25. There will be limited
  staffing for services December 21 through December 23. Non-emergency City
  services will also be closed Friday, January 1, for New Year's Day.

  • Kamlesh "Kam" Chitalia, Chief Building Official, would be retiring after 31 years of
  service to our City. In addition, Molly Perry, City Clerk, would be retiring after six
  years as City Clerk and 22 years in public service.

  4.2  CONSIDERATION  OF  A  REQUEST  BY  MAYOR  KHAN  AND
  COUNCILMEMBER KUO REGARDING REVISIONS TO THE CITY
  COUNCIL POLICY/PROCEDURE CONCERNING CITY COUNCIL
  INITIATED AGENDA ITEMS

  This item was agendized at the request of Mayor Khan and
  Councilmember Kuo, who suggested a revision to the City Council Policy/
  Procedure regarding City Council-initiated agenda items be made to
  remove the sunset clause of January 2021, thereby making the policy
  permanent.

  City Attorney Melching provided a brief summary related to the Ralph M.
  Brown Act(Brown Act) and procedures for Roberts Rules of Order, and
  how they impact the existing policy/procedure; and responded to City
  Council questions.

  Council discussion included: noting that the policy/procedure allowed for
  Councilmembers to work more efficiently; reiterated that the existing
  policy/procedure was complaint with the Brown Act; clarified that
  Councilmembers could request support to agendize items under
  "Announcements" at City Council meetings; reiterated unanimous
  support by the City Council in the past related to social justice matters;

  Prepared by the City Clerk's Office  6
 City Council Minutes  December 8. 2020

  expressed concern about a Councilmember's inability to agendize
  matters that may be of importance to community members; noted the
  opportunity that existed for the Mayor to work closely with the City
  Manager to shape the agenda, and suggested that the same opportunity
  be extended to all Councilmembers; and expressed concern about the
  influence of special interests if the policy/procedure was sunset.

  Molly Perry, City Clerk, stated that 91 e-comments had been received, of
  which those received prior to 2 p.m. had been provided to the City Council
  on the dais, and noted that the following e-comments had been received
  after 2 p.m.:

  • Anonymous Resident, who expressed support, but suggested that
  the Mayor also be required to seek support from a colleague to
  ensure an equitable policy.

  • Ling Wang, who expressed opposition.

  • Irvine Taxpayer, who hoped the City Council's protocol would be
  refined with new leadership and Councilmembers; and expressed
  appreciation to the City Council for refining its work to better serve
  the community.

  • Ashok Tahilramani, Irvine resident, who expressed opposition to
  the item, noting the item restricts freedom of speech, is open to
  manipulation and is the opposite of transparency.

  • Rita Cheng, who expressed opposition.

  • Lesley Tan, who expressed opposition, noting that one
  Councilmember's ability to agendize a matter reaching should be
  sufficient enough for further discussion at a City Council meeting.

  • Fang Yuan, who expressed opposition.

  • Kathleen Tahilramani, who expressed opposition, noting that the
  policy was an unnecessary impediment to moving forward items
  that require City Council attention and action.

  • MaryAnn Gaido, Irvine resident, who expressed opposition, and
  urged the City Council to allow the policy to sunset, noting that the
  spirt of respect and equity should be carried out throughout the
  tenure of the new City Council to model an exemplary form of
  democratic public participation.

  Prepared by the City Clerk's Office
 City Council Minutes  December 8. 2020

  • Gene Kaplan, Irvine resident, who expressed opposition, who
  suggested that the policy could prevent the discussion of good
  ideas from being brought forward to the City Council,
  disenfranchises constituents from being heard, and could
  represent collusion that may border on the intent of the Brown Act.

  • Mary Stephens, Irvine resident, who suggested reconsideration
  of the policy and allowing Councilmembers the ability to bring
  focus to their own concerns as well as those of their particular
  constituents.

  • Thomas Wang, who expressed opposition.
